info.name: SmartParking - SPARK-244 Realtime Layout Monitoring (manual verification)
info.description:
# SPARK-244 Realtime operator layout monitoring - manual verification

Exercises the REST surfaces that back the SPARK-244 realtime operator channel on the SPARK-228 operational-layout read path. Route paths, request records, response fields and status codes are taken from the worktree source, not from a summary:

- `src/Services/FacilityService/SmartParking.FacilityService.API/Program.cs` (operational-layout, internal gate slot routes)
- `src/Services/FacilityService/SmartParking.FacilityService.Application/OperationalLayoutProjection.cs` (wire DTO)
- `src/Services/FacilityService/SmartParking.FacilityService.Persistence/PostgresOperationalLayoutReader.cs` (snapshot composition)
- `src/Services/FacilityService/SmartParking.FacilityService.Persistence/OperatorGateSlotStore.cs` (claim/release SQL)
- `src/Services/OperationService/SmartParking.OperationService.API/Controllers/*.cs` and `Persistence/ReservationGateStore.cs` (walk-in outbox writes)
- `src/Services/OperationService/SmartParking.OperationService.Infrastructure/Clients/OperatorIdentityClient.cs` (403 mapping)
- `scripts/database/overlay/realtime-outbox.sql` and `realtime-projection.sql` (DB-only checks)

## Folders

- **00 - Setup (run first)** - login owner/operator/admin/driver, generate `runSuffix` and the walk-in plate values.
- **01 - Operator layout snapshot** - GET operational-layout: site, contract version, metrics, zones, floors, slot visual states.
- **02 - Outbox / idempotency** - drive the walk-in check-in/check-out REST path that writes `outbox_events`; DB-only SQL checks are documented, not executed by Postman.
- **03 - Release-once** - internal claim, then double release: the second `UPDATE` matches zero rows and the slot stays AVAILABLE.
- **04 - Zone-only reserved count** - assert `zoneOnlyReservedCount` and the reader invariant; true zone-level reservation creation is BLOCKED (no source in the code).
- **05 - Operator scope** - assigned/unassigned operator scope reads, the 403 `OPERATOR_LOT_UNASSIGNED` REST mapping, and the role gate.
- **06 - Realtime delivery / latency** - REST read/write latency proxies only. A real SignalR connect/delta/reconnect case is BLOCKED because Postman cannot perform a SignalR/WebSocket handshake.

## Run order

Run folders top to bottom. Folder 00 must run first: it stores all four tokens and generates `runSuffix`. Folder 03 mutates one seeded slot and restores it. Folder 02/06 create walk-in sessions on `seededSiteId` and check them out again.

## Default local ports

- UserService: `http://localhost:5035` (`userServiceUrl`)
- OperationService: `http://localhost:5055` (`reservationServiceUrl`, the SPARK-238 key name)
- FacilityService: `http://localhost:5045` (`baseUrl`)

## SignalR limitation (important)

Postman cannot open the hub at `/ws/parking-lots/{siteId}/layout`. This collection therefore never claims to verify a WebSocket connection. It verifies the REST surfaces around the hub (gate write -> outbox row -> Facility projection -> operational-layout read) and marks every true SignalR case as **BLOCKED** in `SPARK-244-manual-test-guide.md`. Do not fabricate a REST endpoint for the hub.

## Secrets

The environment ships real demo emails and the public seeded driver password. `ownerPassword`, `operatorPassword`, `adminPassword` and `serviceKey` are intentionally empty. See the manual guide for the `.env` keys.

item.name: 02 - Outbox / idempotency
item.description:
REST-observable side of the SPARK-244 outbox. The walk-in check-in writes an outbox_events row in the same transaction as parking_sessions, and check-out writes an OccupancyReleased row. Postman cannot query PostgreSQL, so the DB-only assertions are SQL pre/post conditions, not pm.test assertions.

DB-ONLY SQL (operations-db, run in psql):

-- 1) envelope written by 2.1 (eventType OccupancyChanged, payload.action=checkin_walkin, no slotId)
SELECT event_id, event_type, occurred_at, sequence_number, site_id, payload, published_at
FROM outbox_events
WHERE site_id = '<seededSiteId>'
ORDER BY sequence_number DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- 2) idempotency anchor (Q3/G5): event_id is the primary key and a duplicate insert must fail
SELECT event_id, event_type, processed_at FROM processed_events ORDER BY processed_at DESC LIMIT 10;

-- 3) stored payload for the walk-in session (replace <walkInSessionId>)
SELECT event_id, payload FROM outbox_events
WHERE payload->>'sessionId' = '<walkInSessionId>';

A true duplicate-delivery test (publish the same envelope twice) needs a broker/DB harness and is BLOCKED for Postman; see the manual guide.

item.name: 03 - Release-once
item.description:
REST-observable release idempotency on the internal gate route: the first release flips OCCUPIED -> AVAILABLE, the second matches zero rows and still returns 204. The release-once ledger (occupancy_release_ledger, unique session_id) belongs to the Facility consumer and is DB-only here.

DB-ONLY SQL (facility-db):

-- release-once ledger: one row per session, unique on session_id
SELECT session_id, count(*) AS rows_for_session
FROM occupancy_release_ledger
GROUP BY session_id
HAVING count(*) > 1;   -- must return zero rows

SELECT * FROM occupancy_release_ledger ORDER BY processed_at DESC LIMIT 10;

-- per-slot replay watermark
SELECT slot_id, last_sequence_number FROM slot_sequence_watermarks ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 10;

Driving a real OccupancyReleased event for a reservation requires a seeded reservation and a running producer/consumer pair; see the manual guide (case 03.7, BLOCKED for Postman).

item.name: 04 - Zone-only reserved count
item.description:
Asserts the ZoneCapacityDto field that carries zone-only precision (OperationalLayoutProjection.cs:43-51). The reader sets both allocatedSlotCount and zoneOnlyReservedCount to the same subtree RESERVED count (PostgresOperationalLayoutReader:143-159, OPEN D0-5). There is no zone-level allocation source in the code, so a true zone-only reservation cannot be created through any REST route. That case is BLOCKED and documented in the manual guide.

DB-ONLY diagnostic (facility-db):

SELECT u.name AS zone, s.slot_code, s.physical_state, s.reservation_state
FROM parking_slots s JOIN spatial_units u ON u.id = s.spatial_unit_id
WHERE s.site_id = '<seededSiteId>' AND s.deleted_at IS NULL
ORDER BY u.name, s.slot_code;

item.name: 06 - Realtime delivery / latency
item.description:
REST proxies only. Postman cannot connect to the SignalR hub, so the true delivery path (Operations state change -> outbox -> RabbitMQ -> Facility consumer -> SignalR group site:{siteId}:operators) is NOT exercised here. 6.1 and 6.3 measure REST read and REST write-to-read time; they do not measure the hub. The dev-only p95 <= 2s target (Q4) is BLOCKED without a WebSocket client and at least 20 samples.

Manual SignalR procedure (BLOCKED for Postman): connect a .NET/JS SignalR client to `{{reservationServiceUrl}}/ws/parking-lots/{{seededSiteId}}/layout` with `?access_token=<operator JWT>`, expect `SnapshotRequired`, then trigger an Operations check-in/check-out and timestamp the `SlotStateChanged` / `OccupancyReleased` callback.
